evaluated.name: Distress Charged Profitability
evaluated.expression: SUB(RATIO(oiadp, at), MUL(VOL(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Leverage is only dangerous in proportion to how unstable operating profits are, so the correct haircut to reported profitability is a risk charge equal to earnings volatility scaled by the debt burden; profitability that survives this charge is genuinely durable operating strength.
evaluated.reasoning: This is not the QMJ profitability-plus-safety rank composite: leverage enters only multiplied by earnings volatility, so a highly levered firm with rock-steady profits is barely penalized while a moderately levered firm with swinging profits is penalized heavily, a genuine three-way interaction that neither component nor their additive combination expresses. All terms are asset-scaled and in the same units, so the subtraction is economically interpretable as expected profitability net of a default-risk charge rather than an arbitrary rank blend.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Profit Net of Debt Service Burden
evaluated.expression: SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at))
evaluated.hypothesis: Operating profitability is only free cash for shareholders after interest and near-term debt maturities are covered; the same EBITDA yield is worth far less when a large fraction of it is pre-committed to servicing and rolling debt.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the ROE−ROA wedge entirely, so there is no division by book equity and no sign flip for loss-makers or firms with negative or near-zero equity; all quantities are asset-scaled and strictly comparable. It is also not the additive twin of a leverage sort because only the serviceable portion of debt enters — interest actually paid plus debt actually maturing — so long-dated, cheaply financed leverage is treated as benign while short-dated, expensive leverage directly consumes profitability.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Debt Repayment Capacity Profit
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(act, lct), oiadp), lt), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitability is durable when the firm could retire its obligations from the combination of existing liquid slack and one year of operating profit; the same profit level is worth less when total liabilities dwarf that capacity.
evaluated.reasoning: This changes the quality channel from debt-service flow (interest and maturities) to stock-level solvency measured against liquid working capital, so the numerator interacts profit flow with balance-sheet slack while the denominator scales by the full claim. It is a distinct economic statement from the archive winner — repayment capacity rather than annual coverage — and will show whether the previous alpha came from liquidity risk or from committed-cash-flow drag.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Retained Earnings Corroborated Profit
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), at)), RANK(RATIO(re, at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Current operating profitability is credible only when the firm has actually accumulated earnings over its life; high current margins with little retained earnings signal a transient or first-cycle profit, while deep retained earnings without current profitability signal decay.
evaluated.reasoning: The MIN of two ranks is a strict conjunction, not an additive composite: a firm scores high only if it clears both the current-profit and the cumulative-profit-history bar, so the long leg is exactly "durable operating strength" and neither single-theme sort reproduces it. Retained earnings to assets is a long-horizon persistence proxy that requires no rolling window, so unlike five-year volatility measures it costs no coverage.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Self Funded Profit Improvement
evaluated.expression: SUB(TREND(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5), TREND(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: Improving profitability is high quality when it is achieved while leverage is falling, and low quality when the margin trend is accompanied by rising debt-financed asset growth; the difference in trends isolates organically funded operating improvement.
evaluated.reasoning: This moves the interaction from levels to dynamics — the joint direction of profitability and financing — which no level-based profitability or leverage sort captures. It tests whether the archive's level-based financing adjustment can be strengthened by a flow-of-funds interpretation, at the cost of a five-year window whose coverage impact we can read directly against Signal 1.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Return Spread Over Borrowing Cost
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(ceq, lt)), RATIO(xint, lt)), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitability is only durable operating strength when the return earned on total capital employed exceeds the interest rate the firm actually pays creditors; a levered firm earning less on assets than it pays on liabilities is transferring value to debtholders regardless of its headline margin.
evaluated.reasoning: This is not the archive winner re-scaled: it compares two rates rather than subtracting a cash claim from a profit level, so the quality channel is the realized cost of debt (xint/lt) and the interaction is the sign and size of the economic spread that determines whether leverage adds or destroys shareholder value. Scaling interest by total liabilities rather than by interest-bearing debt keeps the denominator strictly positive for essentially all non-financials, so coverage should be as good as a plain ROA sort.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Internally Financed Capital Base Profit
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), lt)), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: Current operating profitability is more persistent when the productive capital behind it was financed by accumulated earnings and sustained R&D spending rather than by creditors, because internally funded assets carry no fixed claim and reflect a proven history of profitable reinvestment.
evaluated.reasoning: The multiplicative form makes profitability count in proportion to how much of the firm's capital base is self-generated (retained earnings plus five-year cumulative R&D) relative to creditor claims, which is a funding-origin mechanism rather than an accrual or debt-service adjustment. COALESCE treats unreported R&D as genuinely zero spending, so non-innovators are still ranked by retained earnings and no part of the cross-section is mechanically excluded.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Trough Profit Versus Fixed Claims
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(SUB(TS_MIN(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: The relevant test of durable operating strength is whether the firm's worst recent year of profitability would still have covered its committed interest and maturing debt; firms passing this stress test have profits that cannot be extinguished by a normal downturn.
evaluated.reasoning: Replacing the current profit level with its five-year minimum turns the financing adjustment into an explicit downside stress test, so the signal separates firms whose current coverage rests on a cyclical peak from those whose floor clears their claims — a state-dependent mechanism no accruals or cash-profitability measure captures. Both terms remain asset-scaled and unit-consistent, and the trough operator is the sharpest available expression of "persistent" in the economic story.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Persistent Claim Coverage Count
evaluated.expression: TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(oibdp, ADD(xint, dlc)), 0), 5)
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is how reliably, not how amply, operating profit has covered committed interest and maturing debt; a firm that cleared its fixed claims in every one of the last five years has demonstrated persistence that a single high coverage reading cannot.
evaluated.reasoning: Used alone the 0-5 count avoids the scale-mismatch problem that sank the earlier count-weighted rank product, and it converts the archive's best-performing comparison into a pure frequency-of-solvency measure, which is a different statistic from either the current spread or its five-year minimum. Comparing it against the trough version tells us whether the payoff comes from persistence of coverage or from the depth of the worst year.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Stress Coverage With Liquidity Buffer
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(TS_MIN(oibdp, 5), SUB(act, lct)), ADD(xint, dlc)), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: Durability should be measured as how many years of committed claims the firm could service using its worst recent year of operating profit plus its liquid working-capital reserve; a firm whose trough earnings and cash buffer jointly dwarf its interest and maturing debt has profits that cannot be extinguished by a downturn.
evaluated.reasoning: This is not an input substitution into the archive expression: it changes the statistic from an asset-scaled difference to a stock-plus-flow coverage multiple in years, and it adds the liquidity reserve so that trough profitability and balance-sheet slack are joint substitutes for meeting fixed claims. Because the numerator and denominator are both dollar quantities the construct is dimensionally clean, debt-light firms correctly score at the high end, and winsorization caps the near-zero-denominator tail.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Coverage Level Plus Improvement
evaluated.expression: ADD(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Uncommitted profitability is more valuable when it is also rising, because an improving spread of operating profit over fixed claims signals that the firm is earning its way out of its obligations rather than sitting at a static coverage level.
evaluated.reasoning: Rather than summing two separately published anomalies (profitability and debt issuance) as the flagged version did, both legs here are the same profitability-versus-claims interaction measured in level and in first difference, so neither leg is individually a factor-model staple and the combination tests a timing question the archive has not answered. Standardizing each leg with ZSCORE after winsorization fixes the dispersion-mismatch objection so that neither term can mechanically dominate the sort.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Standardized Profit Less Rollover Risk
evaluated.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A given operating margin is worth less when a large share of near-term debt must be refinanced from a thin stock of liquid assets, because funding-market shocks force distressed asset sales or dilution exactly when the profit stream should be capitalized.
evaluated.reasoning: The critique was purely about commensurability, and standardizing each winsorized leg to unit cross-sectional dispersion means the rollover-pressure term can no longer swamp the profitability term, so the sort reflects a true trade-off rather than a rescaled liquidity ratio. The mechanism remains distinct from the archive's interest-cost channel because it prices debt *maturity and liquidity backing* rather than the price of debt.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Standardized Profit Earnings History Floor
evaluated.expression: MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(re, at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable operating strength requires both a high current operating margin and a genuinely accumulated stock of past earnings, and the binding constraint is whichever dimension is weaker on a comparable scale.
evaluated.reasoning: Standardizing both legs to unit dispersion before the MIN is the precise fix for the critic's objection: neither retained-earnings-to-assets nor the operating margin can dominate the minimum by scale alone, so the conjunction binds on either side across the cross-section and the signal cannot collapse into the retained-earnings anomaly. Unlike the gen-1 rank version, ZSCORE preserves the extreme tails that the long-short spread needs, which is why that version had a 2.07 FMB t-stat but no alpha.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Margin Erosion Against Committed Claims
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitability that has fallen well below its own five-year peak while interest and maturing debt remain fixed indicates an eroding franchise whose obligations were sized for profits it no longer earns, and such firms should subsequently underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the flagged construct's symmetric-instability flavor (which duplicated Distress Charged Profitability) with a realized *drawdown from peak* interacted with the committed claim burden, so the fragility comes from deterioration relative to a demonstrated capability rather than from volatility. Critically, the current margin now enters with the sign of the profitability premium — a firm sitting at its own peak scores zero and is never shorted — so the leverage interaction is not forced to fight RMW.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Uncommitted Profit Less Levered Erosion
evaluated.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable operating strength is high current profit relative to committed claims *and* the absence of margin erosion from the firm's own demonstrated peak; the two conditions identify different firms, so a long-short built on both should be stronger than either alone.
evaluated.reasoning: This unites the archive's best long-side channel (profit net of interest and maturing debt, alpha 2.8-3.2%) with its best short-side channel (levered margin erosion, alpha −6.6%) after standardizing each so that the skewed erosion term cannot dominate variance — the precise fix for its flat FMB slope. If both fmb_tstat and ls_talpha exceed the leader, the lesson is that the family's payoff has two economically separate sources and should be built two-sided from here on.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Additive Erosion And Claim Burden
evaluated.expression: ADD(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms whose margins have fallen far below their own recent peak and that simultaneously carry heavy committed claims subsequently underperform, and the two fragility dimensions add rather than requiring multiplicative co-occurrence.
evaluated.reasoning: This isolates one design choice on the archive's largest-alpha signal: whether erosion and claim burden must multiply (co-occur in the same firm) or merely accumulate. Because both legs are standardized, the additive version has far less skew, so if its FMB slope becomes significantly negative while alpha holds near the multiplicative version's, we learn that the earlier flat slope was a distributional artifact rather than evidence against the channel.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Health Weighted Profitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The profitability premium is concentrated among financially healthy firms: a strong operating margin is a claim on future cash flows only if near-term refinancing needs cannot force the firm to liquidate assets first, so profitability should be weighted by refinancing safety rather than merely added to it.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has only tested additive and standardized-difference combinations of profitability and financial health; this is a genuine conditional in which the health rank acts as a bounded [0,1] weight on the standardized profit z-score, so profitability differences matter most where the balance sheet permits them to be harvested. Using RANK for the weight and ZSCORE for the profit level avoids the sign pathology of multiplying two signed z-scores, in which two negatives would spuriously score high.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Industry Relative Profit Less Rollover Risk
evaluated.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Both attainable margins and normal short-term funding structures are set largely by industry technology and inventory cycles, so only within-industry deviations in profitability and in refinancing pressure identify firm-specific durable strength.
evaluated.reasoning: This varies exactly one preprocessing choice on the current archive leader, and the diagnostic value is high: if industry demeaning raises ls_talpha and Sharpe, the leader's spread was partly a static sector bet (asset-light versus inventory-heavy industries) and every subsequent construct should be industry-standardized, whereas if it degrades the result the cross-industry component is genuine risk-pricing information worth keeping. It is a targeted design test on the best-performing mechanism rather than a new mechanism, which is why only one slot is spent on it.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Margin Less Working Capital Intensity
evaluated.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), sale), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Operating profitability is durable and self-funding when each dollar of sales requires little net working capital, because a short cash-conversion cycle means growth finances itself and profits convert to distributable cash without recourse to creditors.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the mismatched debt-price channel for an untested operating-cycle mechanism: the quality leg is the *level* of working capital tied up per dollar of revenue, which is a structural feature of the business model rather than the year's accrual change, so it is not the Sloan adjustment and not a financing ratio. Both legs are winsorized and standardized so the comparison is commensurable, and all inputs (oibdp, act, lct, sale) are broadly reported, so coverage should match the archive norm.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Profit Less Own History Leverage Creep
evaluated.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(lt, at), TS_MIN(RATIO(lt, at), 5)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitability accompanied by liabilities that have crept well above the firm's own five-year minimum is levered and transient, whereas equally profitable firms operating at their own historical low point of indebtedness have improving, durable financial health.
evaluated.reasoning: This drops the retained-earnings/Altman channel entirely and instead applies the own-history distance operator — which produced the archive's largest alpha on the profit side (margin erosion, −6.6%) — to the liability side, giving a firm-specific balance-sheet deterioration measure rather than a static leverage level that is largely set by industry. Because the penalty leg is a within-firm change rather than a cross-sectional level, it should be substantially orthogonal to CMA and to the leverage-based legs already tested, while remaining commensurable through winsorized standardization.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Profit Less Rollover Less Erosion
evaluated.expression: SUB(SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Refinancing pressure and margin erosion are economically distinct fragility routes — one is a funding-market risk, the other a franchise-decay risk — so subtracting both from operating profitability should identify durable strength more sharply than removing either alone.
evaluated.reasoning: The two penalty channels are the archive's best-performing quality legs and are unlikely to be redundant (a cash-rich firm with a decaying franchise has no rollover risk, and an inventory-heavy grower at its own margin peak has no erosion), so their combination tests whether the leader's alpha and the erosion signal's alpha are additive. All three legs are winsorized and standardized to unit dispersion, so no term can dominate the sort by scale, which is what made the earlier unstandardized versions degenerate.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Erosion Weighted Profitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Current profitability deserves credit only from firms that have not been losing margin against fixed obligations; the franchise-decay state should scale the profitability premium rather than be netted against it.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the targeted repair of the archive's largest-alpha but zero-slope signal: mapping levered erosion into a bounded [0,1] rank weight removes its extreme skew (the cause of the flat FMB slope) while preserving its portfolio-relevant ordering, and the same weighting structure already delivered 3.5% alpha with a 2.34 FMB t-stat when applied to rollover risk. If it beats both parents, conditional weighting rather than standardized differencing becomes the preferred structure for the remaining generations.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Profit Less Maturity Concentration
evaluated.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, lt), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What makes near-term debt dangerous for a profitable firm is the concentration of claims falling due relative to all claims — a maturity-structure choice — rather than merely the thinness of liquid assets available to repay it.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a one-input anatomy test of the current leader that distinguishes two economically different readings of dlc/act: liquidity backing versus maturity concentration; because lt is the denominator the leg is scale-free, defined for nearly all firms, and orthogonal to inventory-cycle differences that drive act. The result tells us whether future refinements should push toward liquidity measures or toward debt-structure measures, which is a decision the archive cannot currently make.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Industry Profit Less Absolute Rollover Risk
evaluated.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Attainable margins are technology- and industry-determined, so profitability should be judged against industry peers, whereas refinancing pressure is priced by capital markets on an absolute basis and its cross-industry variation is genuine risk information rather than a nuisance sector tilt.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-3 pair showed that demeaning both legs raised the FMB slope (2.90→3.27) but cut alpha (3.5%→2.8%) and Sharpe (0.30→0.19), which implies the informative demeaning is on the profitability leg while the fragility leg's absolute level carries the abnormal return. This asymmetric standardization is the direct implication of that evidence and should, if the diagnosis is right, dominate both parents on slope and alpha simultaneously.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash Conversion Weighted Coverage
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profit that exceeds committed claims is only credible if it arrives as cash: accrual-inflated earnings cannot service interest or repay maturing debt, so the coverage spread should be weighted by the degree to which reported income is cash-backed.
evaluated.reasoning: This opens the earnings-quality channel that the archive has never tested, but does so as a bounded conditioner on the solvency-adjusted profit spread rather than as an additive accruals leg, so it cannot collapse into the Sloan sort — a firm with pristine cash conversion but no coverage still scores near zero. The mechanism is a genuine interaction: cash conversion matters precisely because the claims are contractual and must be paid in cash.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Supplier Financed Profit Discount
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), act), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Operating profitability that rests on heavy non-debt operating liabilities — stretched payables and accrued expenses funding the working-capital cycle — is lower quality than the same margin earned with self-funded working capital, because operating-liability leverage inflates returns on invested capital while creating claims that tighten precisely when trade creditors reassess the firm.
evaluated.reasoning: This drops the smoothing-knob idea and instead opens a quality channel the archive has never touched: fragility from *operating* liabilities rather than from financial debt, maturity structure, franchise erosion, or accruals, so it is informative regardless of outcome and should be largely orthogonal to the dlc-based legs already tested. It uses the bounded-rank conditioning structure that has produced the archive's best joint results (Health Weighted Profitability: alpha 3.5%, Sharpe 0.28), and all inputs are broadly reported so coverage should hold at the archive norm.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Industry Profit Less Rollover Less Erosion
evaluated.expression: SUB(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable operating strength is a within-industry margin advantage that is not offset by absolute refinancing pressure and not undermined by franchise decay against fixed obligations; the three conditions are economically separate and their evidence should compound.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's two best signals improved along orthogonal axes — industry demeaning of the profitability leg lifted the FMB slope from 2.90 to 3.80, and adding the erosion leg lifted alpha from 3.5% to 3.8% with t from 3.26 to 3.55 — so their union is the single highest-value untested point and directly targets joint strength rather than one metric. Every leg is winsorized and unit-standardized, so the composite cannot be captured by the leg with the fattest tail.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Balance Sheet Accrual Weighted Coverage
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, lct), 1), dp), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profit in excess of committed claims is credible only if it is not manufactured by working-capital accruals net of capital consumption, because contractual interest and maturing debt must be paid in cash rather than in receivables and inventory.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs the specific failure of Cash Conversion Weighted Coverage, whose mechanism produced the archive's best Sharpe (0.44) and 3.7% alpha but whose oancf input cut coverage to 0.080; the balance-sheet accrual definition uses only act, lct and dp, which are reported throughout the sample, so the same economic conditioner should survive at roughly 0.12 coverage. If the statistics hold up with coverage restored, the earnings-quality conditioner becomes a permanent component; if they collapse, the earlier result was a sample-period artifact.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Profit Less Combined Leverage
evaluated.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(dp, at), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The speed at which a margin can be destroyed depends on the product of operating and financial leverage: a capital-intensive cost structure means revenue declines pass straight through to operating profit, and debt then converts that pass-through into insolvency risk, so profitability accompanied by both is the least durable.
evaluated.reasoning: Every fragility leg tested so far has been purely financial (short-term debt, interest, maturity, operating liabilities); this introduces the asset-side cost-structure dimension and multiplies it with debt so that the penalty applies only where the two amplify each other, which is a different economic object than the failed earnings-volatility × leverage charge because it is structural rather than backward-looking. Using dp/at as the operating-leverage proxy keeps the leg contemporaneous and available for the whole sample, so coverage should not fall.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Coverage Level Less Coverage Drawdown
evaluated.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(TS_MAX(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 5), SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at))), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters for durability is the firm's current cushion of profit over committed claims *and* how far that cushion has fallen from its own five-year peak, since a shrinking solvency cushion signals that obligations were sized against profits the firm no longer earns.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has applied the own-history drawdown operator to the raw margin and to leverage separately, but never to the solvency cushion itself, which is the quantity the economic story says must be stable; measuring level and drawdown of the same object also guarantees the two legs are economically commensurable rather than one being a repackaged leverage sort. This is the natural successor to Coverage Level Plus Improvement (alpha 3.3%, t 3.44), replacing a one-year change with a peak-relative deterioration state.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Solvency Gated Profitability Premium
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), INDICATOR(SUB(act, ADD(lct, dlc)), 0))
evaluated.hypothesis: The profitability premium is a claim on future distributable cash and is only harvestable where the balance sheet cannot force intervention: among firms whose liquid assets exceed all current obligations including maturing debt, margin differences should predict returns, whereas among firms failing that test returns are dominated by distress dynamics and profitability carries little information.
evaluated.reasoning: Unlike a rank product, this is not a monotone re-weighting that collapses toward an additive combination — it is a regime switch that sets the profitability bet to exactly zero for firms failing the liquidity test, so the long and short legs are both drawn from the solvent subsample and the signal makes no profitability bet at all inside the distressed regime. The gate is a genuine accounting inequality (act versus lct plus dlc) rather than a tuned threshold, and it directly tests the archive's central premise that profitability information is conditional on financial health rather than merely additive with it.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Profit Less Maturity Shortening
evaluated.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, lt), 1), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: When creditors shorten a firm's funding — the share of claims coming due within a year rises — they are signalling reduced confidence in the durability of its cash flows, so profitability accompanied by maturity shortening is transient while equally profitable firms that are terming out their obligations have creditor-certified durability.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the erosion-times-leverage family entirely and introduces a credit-supply mechanism: the *change* in maturity composition rather than any level of debt, erosion, or liquidity, which makes it largely orthogonal to CMA, to the static dlc legs already tested, and to the failed own-history leverage creep measure (a level-of-liabilities concept, not a composition concept). The static version of this channel is already productive (Profit Less Maturity Concentration: fmb 2.59, alpha 3.2%, coverage 0.144), so testing its first difference isolates whether creditors' revisions carry information beyond the standing structure.
evaluated.author: proposer

considered.reasoning: This puts profitability on the revenue-side channel (gross profit to assets) and quality on the durability of the margin itself (five-year volatility of gross margin), a mechanism distinct from ROA volatility or cash backing. considered.expression: MIN(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3), MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))

considered.reasoning: Replacing the 0/1 gate with a MIN operator removes the indicator-dominance problem and, critically, is not the accruals anomaly: the accruals signal is the signed difference and goes long firms with low earnings but high cash flow, whereas this lower envelope refuses to reward either channel unless the other confirms it, so cash-rich low-earnings firms score low too. Three-year averaging keeps the concept about persistent dual-channel profitability rather than one-year accrual noise, and coverage stays high because only three annual observations of standard items are required.

considered.hypothesis: Leverage is only dangerous in proportion to how unstable operating profits are, so the correct haircut to reported profitability is a risk charge equal to earnings volatility scaled by the debt burden; profitability that survives this charge is genuinely durable operating strength.
considered.reasoning: This is not the QMJ profitability-plus-safety rank composite: leverage enters only multiplied by earnings volatility, so a highly levered firm with rock-steady profits is barely penalized while a moderately levered firm with swinging profits is penalized heavily, a genuine three-way interaction that neither component nor their additive combination expresses. considered.name: Profit Net of Debt Service Burden
considered.expression: SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at))
considered.hypothesis: Operating profitability is only free cash for shareholders after interest and near-term debt maturities are covered; the same EBITDA yield is worth far less when a large fraction of it is pre-committed to servicing and rolling debt.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the ROE−ROA wedge entirely, so there is no division by book equity and no sign flip for loss-makers or firms with negative or near-zero equity; all quantities are asset-scaled and strictly comparable. It is also not the additive twin of a leverage sort because only the serviceable portion of debt enters — interest actually paid plus debt actually maturing — so long-dated, cheaply financed leverage is treated as benign while short-dated, expensive leverage directly consumes profitability.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Debt Repayment Capacity Profit
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(act, lct), oiadp), lt), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Profitability is durable when the firm could retire its obligations from the combination of existing liquid slack and one year of operating profit; the same profit level is worth less when total liabilities dwarf that capacity.
considered.reasoning: This changes the quality channel from debt-service flow (interest and maturities) to stock-level solvency measured against liquid working capital, so the numerator interacts profit flow with balance-sheet slack while the denominator scales by the full claim. It is a distinct economic statement from the archive winner — repayment capacity rather than annual coverage — and will show whether the previous alpha came from liquidity risk or from committed-cash-flow drag.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Retained Earnings Corroborated Profit
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), at)), RANK(RATIO(re, at)))
considered.hypothesis: Current operating profitability is credible only when the firm has actually accumulated earnings over its life; high current margins with little retained earnings signal a transient or first-cycle profit, while deep retained earnings without current profitability signal decay.
considered.reasoning: The MIN of two ranks is a strict conjunction, not an additive composite: a firm scores high only if it clears both the current-profit and the cumulative-profit-history bar, so the long leg is exactly "durable operating strength" and neither single-theme sort reproduces it. Retained earnings to assets is a long-horizon persistence proxy that requires no rolling window, so unlike five-year volatility measures it costs no coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Self Funded Profit Improvement
considered.expression: SUB(TREND(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5), TREND(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 5))
considered.hypothesis: Improving profitability is high quality when it is achieved while leverage is falling, and low quality when the margin trend is accompanied by rising debt-financed asset growth; the difference in trends isolates organically funded operating improvement.
considered.reasoning: This moves the interaction from levels to dynamics — the joint direction of profitability and financing — which no level-based profitability or leverage sort captures. It tests whether the archive's level-based financing adjustment can be strengthened by a flow-of-funds interpretation, at the cost of a five-year window whose coverage impact we can read directly against Signal 1.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Return Spread Over Borrowing Cost
considered.expression: WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(ceq, lt)), RATIO(xint, lt)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Profitability is only durable operating strength when the return earned on total capital employed exceeds the interest rate the firm actually pays creditors; a levered firm earning less on assets than it pays on liabilities is transferring value to debtholders regardless of its headline margin.
considered.reasoning: This is not the archive winner re-scaled: it compares two rates rather than subtracting a cash claim from a profit level, so the quality channel is the realized cost of debt (xint/lt) and the interaction is the sign and size of the economic spread that determines whether leverage adds or destroys shareholder value. Scaling interest by total liabilities rather than by interest-bearing debt keeps the denominator strictly positive for essentially all non-financials, so coverage should be as good as a plain ROA sort.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Internally Financed Capital Base Profit
considered.expression: WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), lt)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Current operating profitability is more persistent when the productive capital behind it was financed by accumulated earnings and sustained R&D spending rather than by creditors, because internally funded assets carry no fixed claim and reflect a proven history of profitable reinvestment.
considered.reasoning: The multiplicative form makes profitability count in proportion to how much of the firm's capital base is self-generated (retained earnings plus five-year cumulative R&D) relative to creditor claims, which is a funding-origin mechanism rather than an accrual or debt-service adjustment. COALESCE treats unreported R&D as genuinely zero spending, so non-innovators are still ranked by retained earnings and no part of the cross-section is mechanically excluded.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Trough Profit Versus Fixed Claims
considered.expression: WINSOR(SUB(TS_MIN(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: The relevant test of durable operating strength is whether the firm's worst recent year of profitability would still have covered its committed interest and maturing debt; firms passing this stress test have profits that cannot be extinguished by a normal downturn.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the current profit level with its five-year minimum turns the financing adjustment into an explicit downside stress test, so the signal separates firms whose current coverage rests on a cyclical peak from those whose floor clears their claims — a state-dependent mechanism no accruals or cash-profitability measure captures. Both terms remain asset-scaled and unit-consistent, and the trough operator is the sharpest available expression of "persistent" in the economic story.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Persistent Claim Coverage Count
considered.expression: TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(oibdp, ADD(xint, dlc)), 0), 5)
considered.hypothesis: What matters is how reliably, not how amply, operating profit has covered committed interest and maturing debt; a firm that cleared its fixed claims in every one of the last five years has demonstrated persistence that a single high coverage reading cannot.
considered.reasoning: Used alone the 0-5 count avoids the scale-mismatch problem that sank the earlier count-weighted rank product, and it converts the archive's best-performing comparison into a pure frequency-of-solvency measure, which is a different statistic from either the current spread or its five-year minimum. Comparing it against the trough version tells us whether the payoff comes from persistence of coverage or from the depth of the worst year.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Stress Coverage With Liquidity Buffer
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(TS_MIN(oibdp, 5), SUB(act, lct)), ADD(xint, dlc)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Durability should be measured as how many years of committed claims the firm could service using its worst recent year of operating profit plus its liquid working-capital reserve; a firm whose trough earnings and cash buffer jointly dwarf its interest and maturing debt has profits that cannot be extinguished by a downturn.
considered.reasoning: This is not an input substitution into the archive expression: it changes the statistic from an asset-scaled difference to a stock-plus-flow coverage multiple in years, and it adds the liquidity reserve so that trough profitability and balance-sheet slack are joint substitutes for meeting fixed claims. Because the numerator and denominator are both dollar quantities the construct is dimensionally clean, debt-light firms correctly score at the high end, and winsorization caps the near-zero-denominator tail.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Coverage Level Plus Improvement
considered.expression: ADD(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Uncommitted profitability is more valuable when it is also rising, because an improving spread of operating profit over fixed claims signals that the firm is earning its way out of its obligations rather than sitting at a static coverage level.
considered.reasoning: Rather than summing two separately published anomalies (profitability and debt issuance) as the flagged version did, both legs here are the same profitability-versus-claims interaction measured in level and in first difference, so neither leg is individually a factor-model staple and the combination tests a timing question the archive has not answered. Standardizing each leg with ZSCORE after winsorization fixes the dispersion-mismatch objection so that neither term can mechanically dominate the sort.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Standardized Profit Less Rollover Risk
considered.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: A given operating margin is worth less when a large share of near-term debt must be refinanced from a thin stock of liquid assets, because funding-market shocks force distressed asset sales or dilution exactly when the profit stream should be capitalized.
considered.reasoning: The critique was purely about commensurability, and standardizing each winsorized leg to unit cross-sectional dispersion means the rollover-pressure term can no longer swamp the profitability term, so the sort reflects a true trade-off rather than a rescaled liquidity ratio. The mechanism remains distinct from the archive's interest-cost channel because it prices debt *maturity and liquidity backing* rather than the price of debt.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Standardized Profit Earnings History Floor
considered.expression: MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(re, at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Durable operating strength requires both a high current operating margin and a genuinely accumulated stock of past earnings, and the binding constraint is whichever dimension is weaker on a comparable scale.
considered.reasoning: Standardizing both legs to unit dispersion before the MIN is the precise fix for the critic's objection: neither retained-earnings-to-assets nor the operating margin can dominate the minimum by scale alone, so the conjunction binds on either side across the cross-section and the signal cannot collapse into the retained-earnings anomaly. Unlike the gen-1 rank version, ZSCORE preserves the extreme tails that the long-short spread needs, which is why that version had a 2.07 FMB t-stat but no alpha.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Margin Erosion Against Committed Claims
considered.expression: WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Profitability that has fallen well below its own five-year peak while interest and maturing debt remain fixed indicates an eroding franchise whose obligations were sized for profits it no longer earns, and such firms should subsequently underperform.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the flagged construct's symmetric-instability flavor (which duplicated Distress Charged Profitability) with a realized *drawdown from peak* interacted with the committed claim burden, so the fragility comes from deterioration relative to a demonstrated capability rather than from volatility. Critically, the current margin now enters with the sign of the profitability premium — a firm sitting at its own peak scores zero and is never shorted — so the leverage interaction is not forced to fight RMW.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Uncommitted Profit Less Levered Erosion
considered.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Durable operating strength is high current profit relative to committed claims *and* the absence of margin erosion from the firm's own demonstrated peak; the two conditions identify different firms, so a long-short built on both should be stronger than either alone.
considered.reasoning: This unites the archive's best long-side channel (profit net of interest and maturing debt, alpha 2.8-3.2%) with its best short-side channel (levered margin erosion, alpha −6.6%) after standardizing each so that the skewed erosion term cannot dominate variance — the precise fix for its flat FMB slope. If both fmb_tstat and ls_talpha exceed the leader, the lesson is that the family's payoff has two economically separate sources and should be built two-sided from here on.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Additive Erosion And Claim Burden
considered.expression: ADD(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms whose margins have fallen far below their own recent peak and that simultaneously carry heavy committed claims subsequently underperform, and the two fragility dimensions add rather than requiring multiplicative co-occurrence.
considered.reasoning: This isolates one design choice on the archive's largest-alpha signal: whether erosion and claim burden must multiply (co-occur in the same firm) or merely accumulate. Because both legs are standardized, the additive version has far less skew, so if its FMB slope becomes significantly negative while alpha holds near the multiplicative version's, we learn that the earlier flat slope was a distributional artifact rather than evidence against the channel.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Health Weighted Profitability
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: The profitability premium is concentrated among financially healthy firms: a strong operating margin is a claim on future cash flows only if near-term refinancing needs cannot force the firm to liquidate assets first, so profitability should be weighted by refinancing safety rather than merely added to it.
considered.reasoning: The archive has only tested additive and standardized-difference combinations of profitability and financial health; this is a genuine conditional in which the health rank acts as a bounded [0,1] weight on the standardized profit z-score, so profitability differences matter most where the balance sheet permits them to be harvested. Using RANK for the weight and ZSCORE for the profit level avoids the sign pathology of multiplying two signed z-scores, in which two negatives would spuriously score high.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Industry Relative Profit Less Rollover Risk
considered.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Both attainable margins and normal short-term funding structures are set largely by industry technology and inventory cycles, so only within-industry deviations in profitability and in refinancing pressure identify firm-specific durable strength.
considered.reasoning: This varies exactly one preprocessing choice on the current archive leader, and the diagnostic value is high: if industry demeaning raises ls_talpha and Sharpe, the leader's spread was partly a static sector bet (asset-light versus inventory-heavy industries) and every subsequent construct should be industry-standardized, whereas if it degrades the result the cross-industry component is genuine risk-pricing information worth keeping. It is a targeted design test on the best-performing mechanism rather than a new mechanism, which is why only one slot is spent on it.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Margin Less Working Capital Intensity
considered.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), sale), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Operating profitability is durable and self-funding when each dollar of sales requires little net working capital, because a short cash-conversion cycle means growth finances itself and profits convert to distributable cash without recourse to creditors.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the mismatched debt-price channel for an untested operating-cycle mechanism: the quality leg is the *level* of working capital tied up per dollar of revenue, which is a structural feature of the business model rather than the year's accrual change, so it is not the Sloan adjustment and not a financing ratio. Both legs are winsorized and standardized so the comparison is commensurable, and all inputs (oibdp, act, lct, sale) are broadly reported, so coverage should match the archive norm.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profit Less Own History Leverage Creep
considered.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(lt, at), TS_MIN(RATIO(lt, at), 5)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Profitability accompanied by liabilities that have crept well above the firm's own five-year minimum is levered and transient, whereas equally profitable firms operating at their own historical low point of indebtedness have improving, durable financial health.
considered.reasoning: This drops the retained-earnings/Altman channel entirely and instead applies the own-history distance operator — which produced the archive's largest alpha on the profit side (margin erosion, −6.6%) — to the liability side, giving a firm-specific balance-sheet deterioration measure rather than a static leverage level that is largely set by industry. Because the penalty leg is a within-firm change rather than a cross-sectional level, it should be substantially orthogonal to CMA and to the leverage-based legs already tested, while remaining commensurable through winsorized standardization.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profit Less Rollover Less Erosion
considered.expression: SUB(SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Refinancing pressure and margin erosion are economically distinct fragility routes — one is a funding-market risk, the other a franchise-decay risk — so subtracting both from operating profitability should identify durable strength more sharply than removing either alone.
considered.reasoning: The two penalty channels are the archive's best-performing quality legs and are unlikely to be redundant (a cash-rich firm with a decaying franchise has no rollover risk, and an inventory-heavy grower at its own margin peak has no erosion), so their combination tests whether the leader's alpha and the erosion signal's alpha are additive. All three legs are winsorized and standardized to unit dispersion, so no term can dominate the sort by scale, which is what made the earlier unstandardized versions degenerate.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Erosion Weighted Profitability
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Current profitability deserves credit only from firms that have not been losing margin against fixed obligations; the franchise-decay state should scale the profitability premium rather than be netted against it.
considered.reasoning: This is the targeted repair of the archive's largest-alpha but zero-slope signal: mapping levered erosion into a bounded [0,1] rank weight removes its extreme skew (the cause of the flat FMB slope) while preserving its portfolio-relevant ordering, and the same weighting structure already delivered 3.5% alpha with a 2.34 FMB t-stat when applied to rollover risk. If it beats both parents, conditional weighting rather than standardized differencing becomes the preferred structure for the remaining generations.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profit Less Maturity Concentration
considered.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, lt), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: What makes near-term debt dangerous for a profitable firm is the concentration of claims falling due relative to all claims — a maturity-structure choice — rather than merely the thinness of liquid assets available to repay it.
considered.reasoning: This is a one-input anatomy test of the current leader that distinguishes two economically different readings of dlc/act: liquidity backing versus maturity concentration; because lt is the denominator the leg is scale-free, defined for nearly all firms, and orthogonal to inventory-cycle differences that drive act. The result tells us whether future refinements should push toward liquidity measures or toward debt-structure measures, which is a decision the archive cannot currently make.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Industry Profit Less Absolute Rollover Risk
considered.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Attainable margins are technology- and industry-determined, so profitability should be judged against industry peers, whereas refinancing pressure is priced by capital markets on an absolute basis and its cross-industry variation is genuine risk information rather than a nuisance sector tilt.
considered.reasoning: The gen-3 pair showed that demeaning both legs raised the FMB slope (2.90→3.27) but cut alpha (3.5%→2.8%) and Sharpe (0.30→0.19), which implies the informative demeaning is on the profitability leg while the fragility leg's absolute level carries the abnormal return. This asymmetric standardization is the direct implication of that evidence and should, if the diagnosis is right, dominate both parents on slope and alpha simultaneously.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Conversion Weighted Coverage
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Profit that exceeds committed claims is only credible if it arrives as cash: accrual-inflated earnings cannot service interest or repay maturing debt, so the coverage spread should be weighted by the degree to which reported income is cash-backed.
considered.reasoning: This opens the earnings-quality channel that the archive has never tested, but does so as a bounded conditioner on the solvency-adjusted profit spread rather than as an additive accruals leg, so it cannot collapse into the Sloan sort — a firm with pristine cash conversion but no coverage still scores near zero. The mechanism is a genuine interaction: cash conversion matters precisely because the claims are contractual and must be paid in cash.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Supplier Financed Profit Discount
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), act), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Operating profitability that rests on heavy non-debt operating liabilities — stretched payables and accrued expenses funding the working-capital cycle — is lower quality than the same margin earned with self-funded working capital, because operating-liability leverage inflates returns on invested capital while creating claims that tighten precisely when trade creditors reassess the firm.
considered.reasoning: This drops the smoothing-knob idea and instead opens a quality channel the archive has never touched: fragility from *operating* liabilities rather than from financial debt, maturity structure, franchise erosion, or accruals, so it is informative regardless of outcome and should be largely orthogonal to the dlc-based legs already tested. It uses the bounded-rank conditioning structure that has produced the archive's best joint results (Health Weighted Profitability: alpha 3.5%, Sharpe 0.28), and all inputs are broadly reported so coverage should hold at the archive norm.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Industry Profit Less Rollover Less Erosion
considered.expression: SUB(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Durable operating strength is a within-industry margin advantage that is not offset by absolute refinancing pressure and not undermined by franchise decay against fixed obligations; the three conditions are economically separate and their evidence should compound.
considered.reasoning: The archive's two best signals improved along orthogonal axes — industry demeaning of the profitability leg lifted the FMB slope from 2.90 to 3.80, and adding the erosion leg lifted alpha from 3.5% to 3.8% with t from 3.26 to 3.55 — so their union is the single highest-value untested point and directly targets joint strength rather than one metric. Every leg is winsorized and unit-standardized, so the composite cannot be captured by the leg with the fattest tail.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Balance Sheet Accrual Weighted Coverage
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, lct), 1), dp), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Profit in excess of committed claims is credible only if it is not manufactured by working-capital accruals net of capital consumption, because contractual interest and maturing debt must be paid in cash rather than in receivables and inventory.
considered.reasoning: This repairs the specific failure of Cash Conversion Weighted Coverage, whose mechanism produced the archive's best Sharpe (0.44) and 3.7% alpha but whose oancf input cut coverage to 0.080; the balance-sheet accrual definition uses only act, lct and dp, which are reported throughout the sample, so the same economic conditioner should survive at roughly 0.12 coverage. If the statistics hold up with coverage restored, the earnings-quality conditioner becomes a permanent component; if they collapse, the earlier result was a sample-period artifact.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profit Less Combined Leverage
considered.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(dp, at), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The speed at which a margin can be destroyed depends on the product of operating and financial leverage: a capital-intensive cost structure means revenue declines pass straight through to operating profit, and debt then converts that pass-through into insolvency risk, so profitability accompanied by both is the least durable.
considered.reasoning: Every fragility leg tested so far has been purely financial (short-term debt, interest, maturity, operating liabilities); this introduces the asset-side cost-structure dimension and multiplies it with debt so that the penalty applies only where the two amplify each other, which is a different economic object than the failed earnings-volatility × leverage charge because it is structural rather than backward-looking. Using dp/at as the operating-leverage proxy keeps the leg contemporaneous and available for the whole sample, so coverage should not fall.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Coverage Level Less Coverage Drawdown
considered.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(TS_MAX(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 5), SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at))), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: What matters for durability is the firm's current cushion of profit over committed claims *and* how far that cushion has fallen from its own five-year peak, since a shrinking solvency cushion signals that obligations were sized against profits the firm no longer earns.
considered.reasoning: The archive has applied the own-history drawdown operator to the raw margin and to leverage separately, but never to the solvency cushion itself, which is the quantity the economic story says must be stable; measuring level and drawdown of the same object also guarantees the two legs are economically commensurable rather than one being a repackaged leverage sort. This is the natural successor to Coverage Level Plus Improvement (alpha 3.3%, t 3.44), replacing a one-year change with a peak-relative deterioration state.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Solvency Gated Profitability Premium
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), INDICATOR(SUB(act, ADD(lct, dlc)), 0))
considered.hypothesis: The profitability premium is a claim on future distributable cash and is only harvestable where the balance sheet cannot force intervention: among firms whose liquid assets exceed all current obligations including maturing debt, margin differences should predict returns, whereas among firms failing that test returns are dominated by distress dynamics and profitability carries little information.
considered.reasoning: Unlike a rank product, this is not a monotone re-weighting that collapses toward an additive combination — it is a regime switch that sets the profitability bet to exactly zero for firms failing the liquidity test, so the long and short legs are both drawn from the solvent subsample and the signal makes no profitability bet at all inside the distressed regime. The gate is a genuine accounting inequality (act versus lct plus dlc) rather than a tuned threshold, and it directly tests the archive's central premise that profitability information is conditional on financial health rather than merely additive with it.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profit Less Maturity Shortening
considered.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, lt), 1), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: When creditors shorten a firm's funding — the share of claims coming due within a year rises — they are signalling reduced confidence in the durability of its cash flows, so profitability accompanied by maturity shortening is transient while equally profitable firms that are terming out their obligations have creditor-certified durability.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the erosion-times-leverage family entirely and introduces a credit-supply mechanism: the *change* in maturity composition rather than any level of debt, erosion, or liquidity, which makes it largely orthogonal to CMA, to the static dlc legs already tested, and to the failed own-history leverage creep measure (a level-of-liabilities concept, not a composition concept). The static version of this channel is already productive (Profit Less Maturity Concentration: fmb 2.59, alpha 3.2%, coverage 0.144), so testing its first difference isolates whether creditors' revisions carry information beyond the standing structure.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profit Less Volatile Demand Rollover Risk
considered.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(VOL(GROWTH(sale, 1), 5), RATIO(dlc, act)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Refinancing needs are only dangerous for businesses whose revenues can fall sharply; a firm with volatile demand and near-term debt to roll faces funding withdrawal exactly when its sales dip, whereas a stable-revenue firm can carry the same maturing debt safely.
considered.reasoning: Every fragility leg tested so far has been purely balance-sheet; this introduces demand-side instability from the income statement and multiplies it with the archive's best fragility channel, so the penalty applies only where cash-flow risk and funding risk co-occur. It is distinct from the failed earnings-volatility × total-debt charge because the risk is measured on revenue (the exogenous driver) and paired with the *maturing* rather than total debt, which is the claim that actually forces a funding decision.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cumulative Earning Power Versus Claims
considered.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(oibdp, 5), lt), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The most reliable measure of durable operating strength is how many years of accumulated operating profit it would take to extinguish all creditor claims; five years of realized profit relative to total liabilities captures persistence and financial health jointly in a way a single-year margin cannot.
