It uses the quality theme's preferred VOL operator on the archive's most productive fragility variable, and because the level of exposure is deliberately excluded, a strong result would identify capital-access instability rather than leverage as the mechanism.
considered.author: proposer

critic_notes.rationale: The "profitability per unit of profitability instability" ratio is a coherent quality-scaled profitability construct rather than a literal rediscovery, but it sits close to the published earnings-volatility/QMJ-stability literature and the raw ratio will be dominated by near-zero-denominator outliers, so it should be winsorized or rank-transformed before the FMB slope is believed.

Since the 0/1 indicator dominates the [0,1] rank, the sort effectively becomes "negative-accrual firms long, all positive-accrual firms short," making this a repackaging of the Sloan accruals anomaly rather than a genuine profitability-quality interaction.

A rank-product of high profitability and low leverage is the textbook profitability-plus-safety composite (QMJ), offers no mechanism beyond its two well-documented components, and is trivially constructed.

The 0–5 profitable-year count both dwarfs the [0,1] ROA rank (so the signal is mostly a coarse loss-history screen, a known effect) and saturates at 5 for most surviving firms, plus the window length is ambiguous if the panel is monthly with annual data carried forward.

Pairing Novy-Marx gross profitability with the durability of the gross margin itself is an economically motivated moat proxy on a distinct (revenue-side) channel from ROA-volatility variants, though its incremental content versus the Operating Profit Sharpe proposal must be checked and the five-year window will cost coverage.

The ROE–ROA wedge equals ib·(at−ceq)/(ceq·at), so it flips sign for loss-makers (rewarding highly levered unprofitable firms) and explodes for near-zero or negative book equity; absent those pathologies it reduces to roughly "ROA rank minus leverage rank," i.e., the additive twin of the Unlevered Profit Strength proposal.

critic_notes.target_name: Operating Income Net Of Debt Service
critic_notes.rationale: In Compustat `oibdp` is definitionally `revt − cogs − xsga`, so this is the archive winner "Profit Net of Debt Service Burden" re-expressed with a winsorizer — a cosmetic variant whose only genuine content is a data-availability/outlier robustness check, not a new mechanism.

The stock-solvency framing (working-capital slack plus one year of profit against total liabilities) is a defensible economic alternative to the flow-coverage archive signal, though it is close in spirit to the classic Altman Z-score components and the unwinsorized `lt` denominator will blow up for low-liability firms, so the outlier control should be inside the ratio rather than absent.

The MIN-of-ranks conjunction is a genuinely non-additive combination that neither parent sort reproduces and the expected sign matches the construction, but both legs are individually published anomalies (gross/operating profitability and retained-earnings-to-assets à la Ball–Gerakos–Linnainmaa–Nikolaev), so the incremental content rests entirely on the nonlinearity and should be benchmarked against a simple average of the same two ranks.

The trend-difference moves the interaction from levels to dynamics and is internally consistent in sign and units, but the leverage-trend leg is a slow-moving proxy for the well-documented net debt issuance/financing anomaly, and the unstandardized subtraction implicitly assumes the two trends have comparable cross-sectional dispersion — worth testing, but the decomposition into each leg should be reported to show the interaction adds anything.

Operating profit minus the change in net working capital, both scaled by assets, is essentially the Sloan (1996) accrual adjustment and reproduces cash-based operating profitability (Ball et al. 2016); the reasoning's claim that it is "distinct from the signed accruals anomaly" is not supported by the expression, which is exactly earnings-less-working-capital-accruals.

This applies a single mechanical demeaning transform to an already-evaluated archive signal without changing the mechanism, which is precisely the kind of cosmetic variant the objective warns against; industry adjustment is better folded in as a standard preprocessing choice tested alongside a substantively new construct than proposed as a standalone signal.

critic_notes.target_name: Trough Cash Flow Versus Fixed Claims
critic_notes.rationale: This is a single-input substitution (oancf for oibdp) inside the archive's existing winning expression, i.e. a cosmetic variant of "Trough Profit Versus Fixed Claims" rather than a substantively different mechanism, and it additionally imports a well-known cash-flow-coverage/distress measure while cutting sample depth (oancf availability plus a 5-year window) on already-thin 12% coverage.

critic_notes.target_name: Profit Not Funded By New Debt
critic_notes.rationale: Economically coherent and dimensionally consistent, but it is essentially an unweighted sum of two separately published anomalies (operating profitability and net debt issuance/asset growth), both of which are heavily spanned by RMW and CMA, so any FF5 alpha is likely to be small — and the equal-weight subtraction of legs with very different cross-sectional dispersion means whichever leg dominates variance will drive the sort.

The two legs are not commensurable — oibdp/at has a standard deviation of roughly 0.1 while dlc/act is fat-tailed and can exceed 1 — so the difference is dominated by the penalty term and the signal degenerates into a rescaled short-term-debt-to-current-assets liquidity ratio (a standard Altman-style distress input) rather than the claimed profit-net-of-rollover construct.

In raw asset-scaled units re/at is far more dispersed and far more often deeply negative than oibdp/at, so the MIN will equal re/at for the large majority of firms and especially throughout the short leg — the signal collapses into the known retained-earnings-to-assets anomaly and the stated "binding constraint" conjunction is illusory, which is precisely why the earlier rank version was constructed that way.

A genuinely different statistic (frequency rather than depth of fixed-claim coverage) with a scale-free level-vs-level comparison and a clear diagnostic contrast against the trough version, though the six-valued support will likely pile most firms at 5 and yield a coarse, unstable top-quintile composition that caps its portfolio power.

Isolating the short leg is a legitimate and underexplored move, but "distance above own five-year profit trough × liability intensity" is close to the earnings-instability × debt-burden penalty term already tested as Distress Charged Profitability (fmb 1.74, ls_talpha 1.49), and the expected negative sign puts the level-of-profitability component of the interaction in direct opposition to the well-documented profitability premium, so the leverage interaction must carry essentially all of the signal.

Internally consistent (subtracting a negatively-signed erosion leg yields the stated positive sign) and it deliberately pairs the archive's strongest long-side and short-side channels on a common scale, though the erosion leg's near-zero FMB slope means the cross-sectional gain may be diluted even if the portfolio alpha improves.

A legitimate and cleanly specified decomposition test of whether the erosion signal's alpha requires multiplicative co-occurrence, but half the composite (interest+current debt over assets) is essentially a standard leverage/debt-burden sort, so a negative result would be hard to attribute and a positive one partly rediscovers leverage.

The bounded-rank weighting genuinely implements "profitability premium concentrated among healthy firms" and avoids the two-negatives pathology as claimed, but note the construction pushes healthy-yet-unprofitable firms into the extreme short leg while compressing distressed firms toward the middle, which is a real economic bet the hypothesis never defends.

The hypothesis claims to measure the rate creditors charge, but xint/lt divides interest by total liabilities including non-interest-bearing payables and accruals, so the leg is dominated by debt intensity rather than debt price — a hypothesis/expression mismatch that also makes this a lightly restandardized rerun of the already-weak Return Spread Over Borrowing Cost.

Retained-earnings-scaled-by-claims plus profitability is a near-rediscovery of the Altman RE/TA distress component combined with the standard profitability premium, and the only differences from the archive's two already-failed retained-earnings constructs are the denominator (lt vs at) and MIN→ADD, which is too thin a variation to justify a slot.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry Relative Profit Less Rollover Risk
critic_notes.rationale: This is a one-knob preprocessing variant of the current leader rather than a new mechanism, which borders on cosmetic, but industry demeaning of both legs is a genuinely informative test of whether the leader's spread is a static sector tilt, and the result would discipline all subsequent constructs.

Internally consistent and correctly scaled, but it is a mechanical third-leg stack of two archive legs — and the erosion leg's near-zero FMB slope (-0.15) makes it likely to dilute the leader's cross-sectional t-stat while adding little independent alpha, so the informational payoff is modest.

A defensible re-shaping of the skewed erosion leg into a bounded conditioner, but the structure inherits a real sign pathology already latent in Health Weighted Profitability — multiplying a signed z-score by a positive rank weight means unprofitable firms are penalized *more* for having low erosion — so any result will be hard to interpret as evidence for the stated conditional mechanism.

This is only a denominator swap on one leg of the leader, but act→lt changes the leg's economic content from liquidity backing to maturity concentration and yields a diagnostic the archive genuinely cannot currently resolve, so it is a legitimate if narrow anatomy test.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry Profit Less Absolute Rollover Risk
critic_notes.rationale: The asymmetric demeaning is the correct and specific implication of the observed slope-up/alpha-down divergence between the two gen-3 parents, the expected sign matches the expression's natural direction, and the test cleanly separates which leg's cross-industry variation is priced versus nuisance.

It opens a genuinely untested earnings-quality channel and is not a bare accruals sort, but (ib − oancf)/at is exactly the Sloan cash-flow accrual measure so part of any result will be the known accruals premium, and the signed-z-score × positive-rank construction again perversely rewards weak cash conversion among negative-coverage firms; oancf availability may also cut coverage.

This is a pure smoothing-window knob on the existing leader with no new economic content — precisely the cosmetic parameter variant the objective warns against — and three-year averaging of annual accounting ratios is very likely to produce a near-collinear signal rather than a diagnostic about durability.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry Profit Less Rollover Less Erosion
critic_notes.rationale: The expression correctly implements the stated three-leg logic and sign, but it is a mechanical union of two already-tested archive winners rather than a new economic mechanism, so the informational payoff is incremental and the industry-demeaned profit leg plus absolute leverage legs risk importing a residual sector tilt that inflates the FMB slope without new alpha.

The coverage-restoration motive is legitimate and the expression matches the hypothesis, but the conditioner is close to the published Sloan balance-sheet accrual measure (and mismeasured, since DELTA(act−lct) includes cash and short-term debt changes), and the signed-z × rank product retains the pathology that safe firms with negative coverage are pushed further down the ranking.

A product of two [0,1] ranks is empirically almost indistinguishable from their sum, so this is a cosmetic re-parameterization of the already-tested Health Weighted Profitability / profit-minus-rollover pair and cannot cleanly isolate "real interaction" from an additive combination of profitability and liquidity.

This is the first proposal to introduce an asset-side cost-structure dimension and the expression and sign are internally consistent, though the reviewer should note that dp/at is mechanically positively related to oibdp/at (EBITDA is pre-depreciation), so part of any result may reflect de-biasing of the profitability leg rather than the claimed operating × financial leverage amplification.

Economically coherent and correctly signed, but because the current coverage term appears in both legs the composite algebraically reduces to roughly twice the coverage level minus its five-year peak, making it substantially redundant with the already-tested coverage-level signals and mechanically penalizing firms that were once highly profitable.

This swaps one leverage partner for another inside the already-tested erosion-interaction construct, which is a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the zero-inflated nonnegative product means the short leg is again driven by the same subset of peak-fallen levered firms.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry Profit Less Rollover Less Recent Decay
critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially the gen-5 leader with the lookback on one of its three legs shortened from five years to one (SUB(LAG(x,1),x) is just the negative one-year DELTA already used in "Coverage Level Plus Improvement"), so despite the plausible staleness story it reads as a window-parameter variant rather than a substantively new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Profit Less Volatile Demand Rollover Risk
critic_notes.rationale: Genuinely introduces a demand-side (revenue volatility) risk source absent from the entirely balance-sheet fragility legs tested so far, the interaction with *maturing* rather than total debt is economically well-argued and distinct from the failed earnings-vol × total-debt charge, and the sign convention matches the expression — the main risk is skew and coverage loss from the six-year VOL(GROWTH) window.

critic_notes.target_name: Profit Less Rollover Less Trade Credit Reliance
critic_notes.rationale: The two fragility legs are algebraically near-complementary — dlc/act plus (lct−dlc)/act equals lct/act — so the composite largely collapses to industry-relative margin minus the inverse current ratio, undermining the claim that the legs diversify across economically independent creditor types.

Replacing the one-year asset-scaled margin with cumulative five-year profit over total liabilities is a defensible persistence-plus-solvency reformulation that overlaps but is not identical to the earlier "Debt Repayment Capacity Profit," though mixing five years of stale flows against a current liability stock invites stale-information decay and the profitability leg loses the industry adjustment that drove the best archive results.

critic_notes.target_name: Bottom Line Profit Less Rollover Risk
critic_notes.rationale: This is a single-ingredient swap (pi for oibdp) whose stated purpose is to confirm a null — the reasoning predicts the signal will be *worse*, which sits awkwardly with EXPECTED_SIGN positive — and pi/at is simply the well-known ROA anomaly bolted onto an existing leg, making it an ablation diagnostic rather than a candidate signal.

critic_notes.target_name: Profit With History Position Less Rollover
critic_notes.rationale: Substituting a bounded own-history TS_RANK for the zero-inflated peak-drawdown product is a legitimate statistical repair with a clear diagnostic prediction, but adding it to the contemporaneous margin level introduces substantial redundancy with that level, so a large incremental gain over the two-leg industry-profit-less-rollover benchmark is unlikely.

critic_notes.target_name: Innovation Profit Less Rollover Less Idiosyncratic Decay
critic_notes.rationale: Internally consistent (the NEG(IND_ADJ(DELTA)) leg correctly penalizes idiosyncratic margin decline) and the sign logic holds, but it is a mechanical union of two already-tested archive signals rather than a new economic idea, so its informational value is limited to confirming whether the two adjustments are additive.

critic_notes.target_name: Profit Plus Research Intensity Less Rollover
critic_notes.rationale: The unbundling diagnostic is legitimate and answers a real question about the gen-6 jump, but the freed R&D/assets leg is close to the published R&D-intensity premium, and COALESCE(xrd,0) conflates non-reporters with zero-R&D firms, so a positive result will be hard to attribute to the intended mechanism.

Construction is internally inconsistent — R&D sits below the gross-profit line (typically inside xsga), so revt−cogs never deducted it and adding xrd back double-credits research spending, on top of the profit leg being essentially the published gross-profitability anomaly.

A genuinely new and economically coherent interaction (forced abandonment of intangible investment under refinancing pressure) with the penalty correctly zero for non-innovators, though replacing rather than supplementing the standalone rollover leg risks discarding the archive's most reliable penalty for the ~half of firms with no R&D.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Plus Research Profit Less Rollover
critic_notes.rationale: Consistent construction (oancf does expense R&D, so the add-back is not double-counting) and a substantive test of whether the cash/accrual distinction is separate from the investment-measurement correction, with the acknowledged caveat that it partly overlaps the published cash-based operating profitability factor and will face reduced coverage.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry Cumulative Earning Power Less Rollover
critic_notes.rationale: Economically coherent and the liabilities denominator makes it more than a cosmetic tweak, but it is largely an archived signal (Cumulative Earning Power Versus Claims) with two already-proven adjustments bolted on, so the expected marginal learning is modest and any gain may reflect the leverage-scaled denominator rather than the persistence channel.

critic_notes.target_name: Full Sample Cash Innovation Profit Composite
critic_notes.rationale: The expression is a straightforward stack of two already-tested archive legs (cash+R&D-over-assets vs. rollover, plus idiosyncratic decay) whose only genuine innovation is the FFO fallback for missing oancf, so it is close to incremental — but the coverage repair is economically defensible and the three-leg combination has not literally been run, making it worth one confirmatory test rather than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Full Sample Cash Profit Less Rollover
critic_notes.rationale: This is the archive's "Cash Plus Research Profit Less Rollover" with a missing-data fill and nothing else, i.e. a robustness/coverage variant of an existing signal rather than a new cross-theme hypothesis, and its stated diagnostic purpose is already served by comparing Signal 1 with the existing gen-7 entries.

critic_notes.target_name: Innovation Profit With Sustained Research Less Rollover
critic_notes.rationale: TS_COUNT(xrd,5) counts non-missing R&D reports, so the added leg is effectively a near-binary "is an R&D-reporting firm" indicator (mass at 0 and 5) standardized cross-sectionally rather than within industry — it prices sector membership, survivorship of five years of data, and disclosure practice, not the "funded commitment persistence" the hypothesis claims, and it therefore does not resolve the COALESCE-conflation concern it was designed to address.

critic_notes.target_name: Innovation Profit Less Rollover Less Funding Risk
critic_notes.rationale: The hierarchical test (supplement rather than replace the general rollover penalty) is a legitimate and well-diagnosed response to the gen-7 alpha loss, but the stated justification is wrong — after WINSOR/ZSCORE the zero-R&D firms receive a common negative z-score, so the extra leg adds a systematic level bonus to non-innovators and partly undoes the numerator's R&D add-back rather than "only refining ordering within the research-intensive part."

This is a genuine internal-consistency correction — the archive leader penalizes unadjusted EBITDA decay while rewarding R&D-inclusive profitability, mechanically punishing firms that step up research — and the comparison cleanly identifies whether the mismatch was an expense-discipline signal or measurement error.

critic_notes.target_name: Innovation Profit Less Chronic Rollover Exposure
critic_notes.rationale: Peak five-year refinancing exposure is a distinct and untested state variable in this archive with a coherent creditor-run rationale, though the operator (single worst year) does not match the "chronic dependence across the cycle" language — a trailing average would test the stated mechanism more faithfully — and it will be highly collinear with the current level leg it replaces.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Innovation Profit Less Chronic Rollover Less Coherent Decay
critic_notes.rationale: A coherent but purely mechanical stacking of three legs already validated separately in the archive, and its "full-sample" ambition is undercut by an internal inconsistency — the level leg uses COALESCE(oancf, ib+dp) while the decay leg uses raw oancf, so coverage will still be gated by cash-flow availability.

critic_notes.target_name: Innovation Profit Less Average Rollover Less Coherent Decay
critic_notes.rationale: Swapping TS_MAX(dlc/act,5) for MA(dlc/act,3) is an operator tweak on a highly persistent ratio whose smoothed and peak versions will be near-collinear, so this is a cosmetic variant of two already-tested composites (fmb 5.019 and 4.635) rather than a new economic mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Intangible Capital ROIC Less Chronic Rollover Less Decay
critic_notes.rationale: The consistent-capitalization denominator is a defensible (if Peters-Taylor-adjacent) refinement worth testing inside the leading composite, but the hypothesis's "capitalize on both sides" logic is violated in the decay leg, which still uses oibdp+xrd over unadjusted assets.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Innovation Profit Less Chronic Rollover
critic_notes.rationale: Trivial in construction — a z-score difference of two legs already scored individually, each essentially a known anomaly (cash operating profitability; short-term-debt/rollover reliance) — but it serves a legitimate purpose as the parsimony benchmark against which the three-leg variants must justify their extra complexity.

critic_notes.target_name: Chronic Rollover Penalty With Deleveraging Credit
critic_notes.rationale: The construct is close to algebraically degenerate: −ZSCORE(TS_MAX) + ZSCORE(TS_MAX − current) largely cancels the peak term and collapses toward −ZSCORE(current dlc/act), i.e. a reweighted interpolation between the snapshot-rollover signal (already tested, fmb 4.759) and the chronic one, so the claimed new "distance travelled" dimension is not cleanly identified.

critic_notes.target_name: Smoothed Innovation Profit Less Chronic Rollover Less Decay
critic_notes.rationale: Three-year averaging of the profitability leg is a low-novelty but genuinely untested-in-this-family persistence refinement with a clear turnover/noise rationale, and the explicit decay leg does prevent the smoothing from masking deterioration; expect only marginal metric movement.
